$doc: Vyomi capability registry — Lambda. See s3.json for the contract.

lambda.invoke.title: Invoke (synchronous and asynchronous)
limitations: Only the Python runtime actually executes: the handler's source runs in a sandboxed interpreter (curated builtins, a stdlib allow-list, no filesystem/network/process access). Node.js/.NET/Java/Ruby runtimes can be selected and stored, but Invoke always runs the stored source as Python.

Event (async) invocation runs the handler immediately rather than queuing it for later delivery — there is no retry/backoff window, so a destination or DLQ always sees the FIRST (and only) attempt's outcome, reported as condition "RetriesExhausted" on failure.

lambda.aliases-versions.title: Aliases and versions
limitations: Weighted alias routing is stored and returned exactly as configured, but Invoke always runs $LATEST/the alias's primary version — Vyomi does not probabilistically split traffic.

lambda.layers.title: Layers
limitations: A layer's content is stored and sized for real, but it is never merged into the sandbox at Invoke time — attaching a layer records the association without changing what the function can import.

lambda.triggers.title: Triggers / event source mappings
limitations: Creating, listing, enabling/disabling and deleting a trigger (SQS, DynamoDB, Kinesis, S3, SNS, EventBridge, API Gateway, CloudWatch Logs) is real and stateful. Vyomi never polls or subscribes the other service, so a trigger never actually invokes the function on its own — LastProcessingResult always reads "No records processed". Only a direct Invoke (Test tab or the native API) runs code.

lambda.concurrency.title: Reserved concurrency
limitations: Setting ReservedConcurrentExecutions to 0 really throttles — every Invoke is rejected with TooManyRequestsException and Throttles increments, exactly as real Lambda does. A positive reservation is stored and returned, but never enforced against concurrent callers — Vyomi runs every Invoke synchronously (nothing to run concurrently), so no invoke is ever rejected for exceeding a nonzero reservation.

lambda.destinations.title: Asynchronous invocation destinations
limitations: On a real async (Event) Invoke, the OnSuccess/OnFailure destination (SQS queue, SNS topic or another Lambda function) really receives the invocation envelope, and a legacy DeadLetterConfig really receives the raw event on failure when no OnFailure destination is set — same precedence and envelope shape as real Lambda. An EventBridge event-bus destination is accepted and stored but never delivered to (counts toward AsyncDeliveryFailures) — Vyomi's cross-core delivery seam only reaches SQS/SNS/Lambda targets.

lambda.vpc-filesystems.title: VPC config and EFS file systems
limitations: SubnetIds/SecurityGroupIds are validated for real: both must be given together (or both omitted, to detach), and each ID must look like a real EC2 resource ID — a malformed or missing pair is rejected with InvalidParameterValueException, exactly as real Lambda rejects it at Create/UpdateFunctionConfiguration time. An EFS access point's Arn and LocalMountPath are format-validated the same way. Vyomi has no shared VPC engine on this seam, so a syntactically valid but nonexistent subnet, security group or file system is still accepted; once a config passes validation it is stored and returned exactly as configured — Vyomi never attaches a real ENI or mounts a real file system, so code never actually reaches the VPC or the file system at Invoke time.

lambda.metrics.title: Monitor tab metrics and recent invocations
limitations: Invocations/Duration/Error metrics and the recent-invocations list are real — computed from the function's actual last 20 Invoke calls — but this is Vyomi's own lightweight read, not a real CloudWatch Logs Insights / X-Ray integration. Throttles and AsyncDeliveryFailures are real running counters (see lambda.concurrency / lambda.destinations); ConcurrentExecutions always reads 0 — Vyomi never runs two invocations of a function at once.

lambda.code-signing.title: Code signing (deploy-time enforcement)
limitations: A function's attached code signing config really gates CreateFunction/UpdateFunctionCode: with the config's validation policy set to Enforce, a deploy is rejected with CodeVerificationFailedException unless it declares a SigningProfileVersionArn that is one of the config's AllowedPublishers; with Warn, an unsigned/untrusted deploy is still allowed, exactly like real Lambda. Vyomi has no AWS Signer integration or cryptographic signature pipeline, so 'signed' means the deploy call declares a trusted signing profile ARN — there is no real signature to forge or verify over the code bytes themselves.

lambda.code-signing-configs.title: Code signing configurations (create, list, update, delete)
limitations: The configuration resource (allowed signing profiles, validation policy) is stored and returned for real, and is enforced against deployments of any function it is attached to (see lambda.code-signing). A code signing config cannot be deleted while still attached to a function — Vyomi rejects that with ResourceConflictException, matching real Lambda.

lambda.capacity-providers.title: Capacity providers
limitations: The capacity provider resource (name, architectures, max vCPU, scaling mode, VPC) is stored and returned for real. It never actually schedules a function onto reserved EC2 instances — Vyomi's Lambda core only has one runtime, the sandboxed serverless one; attaching a capacity provider doesn't change where Invoke runs.

lambda.network-connectors.title: Network connectors
limitations: The connector resource (VPC, protocol, compute type) is stored and returned for real. It never actually bridges network traffic — there is no MicroVM runtime on the other end of the connection (see lambda.microvms).

lambda.microvms.title: MicroVM Images and MicroVMs
limitations: MicroVM images and running MicroVMs are stored and returned for real (name, state, version, status). There is no Firecracker runtime underneath — a MicroVM never actually boots or runs code; it is a tracked resource record only.

lambda.applications.title: Applications
limitations: An application is a tracked deployment record (name, description, status, template) stored and returned for real. Vyomi has no CloudFormation/SAM core, so creating one never actually provisions the underlying Lambda functions, APIs or tables a template would describe — Status always reads CREATE_COMPLETE immediately.

lambda.replicas.title: Replicas (Lambda@Edge)
limitations: A replica record is derived directly from the function it replicates (same Description/Runtime/LastModified) and the region list is stored for real. Vyomi has no CloudFront distribution to deploy a replica to, so a replica is never actually invoked at an edge location — the record is bookkeeping only.

lambda.state-machines-link.title: Step Functions state machines (cross-link)
limitations: Not a Lambda resource — this page lists real Step Functions state machines (core/stepfunctions_core.py) for the console cross-link real AWS Lambda shows; create/execute them for real in the Step Functions console.
